# You've got data to store!

#### Learning objectives {-}

- Get the data safely onto your device or hard drive
- Understand what the output of the data is

&nbsp;

So, you've successfully made a QGIS survey and collected your data. Now onto potentially the most important step of this entire process: making sure that you don't lose all of the data that you just collected. 

## Saving data onto a hard drive {-}
You spent a tough day collecting data in the field, it is now time to store this data in several places to mitigate risks.

**1.** Open the Play Store, type 'fv file manager app' in the research bar and click on *Install* in the right panel.
![](docs/img/ssd_backup1.jpg)
**2.** Once **FV File Manager** is installed, you can click on *Ouvrir*.
![](docs/img/ssd_backup2.jpg)

**3.** In the notification pop-up, click *Don't allow*.
![](docs/img/ssd_backup3.jpg)

**4.** Click *Do not consent* in the personal data use pop-up window.
![](docs/img/ssd_backup4.jpg)

**5.** Click on the *Files* symbol in the right-hand side.

**6.** Connect your hard drive.

**7.** Go to your hard drive location, here *T7 Shield*. Click on the three verticals dots in the right-hand corner and select *New folder* in the drop-down menu.
![](docs/img/ssd_backup6.jpg)

**8.** Give a name with today's date in YYYYMMDD format, for instance *20260112_sauvegarde*. Click *OK*.
![](docs/img/ssd_backup7.jpg)

**9.** Click on *Galaxy Tab Active4 Pro* on the left panel.
![](docs/img/ssd_backup8.jpg)

**10.** Click on *Android* folder.
![](docs/img/ssd_backup9.jpg)


**11.** Click on *data* folder.
![](docs/img/ssd_backup10.jpg)

**12.** Click on *ch.opengis.qfield* folder.
![](docs/img/ssd_backup11.jpg)

**13.** Click on *files* folder.
![](docs/img/ssd_backup12.jpg)

**14.** Click on *Imported projects* folder.
![](docs/img/ssd_backup13.jpg)

**15.** Select `qgis_training_example2` by keeping your finger on it, click on the three dots in the top right corner and click on *Copy to*.
![](docs/img/ssd_backup14.jpg)

**16.** Go to the folder you created at step 8 on your hard drive (today `20260112_sauvegarde`) and click on *COPY* in the bottom left corner.
![](docs/img/ssd_backup15.jpg)

**17.** Your day's work is now safely stored in the hard drive. This step must be repeated every night and on a second hard drive.
![](docs/img/ssd_backup16.jpg)

## Saving data onto a computer {-}
**1.** Go to the tablet `Internal storage` in your computer file explorer and click on the *Android* folder.
![](docs/img/computer_backup1.png)

**2.** Click on *data* folder.
![](docs/img/computer_backup2.png)

**3.** Click on *ch.opengis.qfield* folder.
![](docs/img/computer_backup3.png)

**4.** Click on *files* folder.
![](docs/img/computer_backup4.png)

**5.** Click on *Imported projects* folder.
![](docs/img/computer_backup5.png)

**6.** Copy `qgis_training_example2`.
![](docs/img/computer_backup6.png)

**7.** Go to the folder where you initially created your QGIS project. Create a `dump` folder.
![](docs/img/computer_backup7.png)

**8.** Paste the `qgis_training_example2` from step 6 in the `dump` folder.
![](docs/img/computer_backup8.png)

**9.** Double-click on the QGIS project to open it.
![](docs/img/computer_backup9.png)

**10.** Once QGIS is launched, open the *Extensions* menu, select *QFieldSync* and then *Synchroniser depuis QField*.
![](docs/img/computer_backup10.png)

**11.** Click on the three dots symbol in the top right corner of the pop-up window.
![](docs/img/computer_backup11.png)

**12.** Select the folder you pasted at step 8 then click on *Sélectionner un dossier*.
![](docs/img/computer_backup12.png)

**13.** Click on *Synchronisation*.
![](docs/img/computer_backup13.png)

**14.** Point colours has changed: the data has arrived.
![](docs/img/computer_backup14.png)

**15.** Click right on the *treesheet_training* layer, select *Exporter* and then *Sauvegarder les entités sous...*.
![](docs/img/computer_backup15.png)

**16.** Verify that *XSLX* is selected in the *Format* menu, then click on the three dots symbol.
![](docs/img/computer_backup16.png)

**17.** Write the future file name beginning by today's date, for instance `20260112_qgis_training_example2.xlsx`, then click on *Enregistrer*.
![](docs/img/computer_backup17.png)

**18.** Click *OK*. You can go to the storage location and verify that you got your data back!
![](docs/img/computer_backup18.png)
